readmeHtml:
GitButler


Our beautiful GUI

Our amazing but CLI



GitButler is a powerful new Git-based version control system, designed from scratch to be simple, powerful and flexible. It is designed for ease of use and modern agentic workflows.

It features stacked branches, parallel branches, unlimited undo, easy commit mutations, forge integrations and more.

Works instantly in any existing Git repo as a friendlier and more powerful drop-in Git user interface replacement - for you and your agents.

Why use GitButler instead of vanilla Git? What a great question.

  • Stacked Branches (gui, cli)
    • Effortlessly create branches stacked on other branches. Amend or edit any commit easily with automatic restacking.
  • Parallel Branches (gui, cli)
    • Organize work on multiple branches simultaneously, rather than constantly switching branches.
  • Easy Commit Management (gui, cli)
    • Uncommit, reword, amend, move, split and squash commits by dragging and dropping or simple CLI commands. Forget about rebase -i, you don't need it anymore.
  • Undo Timeline (gui, cli)
    • Logs all operations and changes and allows you to easily undo or revert any operation.
  • First Class Conflicts (gui, cli)
    • Rebases always succeed. Commits can be marked as conflicted and resolved at any time, in any order.
  • Forge Integration (gui, cli)
    • Authenticate to GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket to easily open and update Pull Requests, list branches, get CI statuses and more. No other tools required.
  • AI Tooling (gui, cli)
    • Use built-in AI handlers to help create commit messages, branch names, PR descriptions and more.
    • Easily install hooks or skills for all modern agent systems to level up their Git management.

Documentation

You can find our end user documentation at: https://docs.gitbutler.com

Bugs and Feature Requests

If you have a bug or feature request, feel free to open an issue, or join our Discord server.

License

The TLDR is that GitButler is under a Fair Source software license, meaning that you can use it, view the source, contribute, etc. You just can't build a competitor with it. It also becomes MIT after 2 years. So, MIT with an expiring non-compete clause.

Contributing

So you want to help out? Please check out the CONTRIBUTING.md document.

If you want to skip right to getting the code to actually compile, take a look at the DEVELOPMENT.md file.

releases.name: release/0.23.2
releases.body:
##Fixes

- Fixes commits and amendments disturbing staged files or hiding later file edits
- Fixes problems caused by missing target-branch tracking: older projects failing to open, missing pull request details and skipped remote updates
- Fixes the app not refreshing after external worktree changes and showing errors for worktrees removed outside the app
- Fixes merged pull requests disappearing from worktree branches after updating the workspace
- Fixes undo leaving newly created branches behind or failing to restore deleted branches after Git garbage collection
- GitLab: Fixes merge request listing on older instances and authentication with server URLs ending in `/api/v4/`
- Bitbucket: Fixes pull request creation and browser links for remotes using `ssh.bitbucket.org`
- Creating an independent branch from the target now checks it out without unnecessarily switching to the workspace
- Fixes unstacking failures with linked worktrees and branches disappearing from the native app when unstacked

## CLI

- `but agent setup` now supports Amp; `but agent uninstall` removes GitButler skills and instructions from coding agents
- Claude desktop agents can now enable Auto-fi

releases.name: release/0.23.1
releases.body:
## Fixes

- Fixes projects failing to load after choosing `gitbutler/workspace` as the target branch (a regression from 0.23.0)
- Fixes pushes failing when the target branch has no upstream and the pushed branches have no open pull requests (a regression from 0.23.0)
- Fixes phantom uncommitted changes after staging, renaming or deleting files outside GitButler
- Discarding a file deletion now restores its committed content, even if a different version was staged
- Fixes upstream merge commits showing the wrong pull request title and link
- Fixes worktree removal incorrectly showing a "Worktree … does not exist" error
- Fixes the target branch picker failing with "Expected object of kind commit but got tree" when a remote ref points to a tree

## CLI

- `but pr new` now lets Claude desktop enable Auto-fix for pull requests opened from their checked-out branch
- `but apply --json` no longer includes the `workspaceRefCreated` field
- `but push <branch> --dry-run` now lists every branch that will be pushed, including branches beneath it in the stack
- `but branch` no longer lists the checked-out branch twice after unapplying down to one branch
- `but apply` no longer r

releases.name: release/0.23.0
releases.body:
## Work in any branch without `gitbutler/workspace`

GitButler now works in any Git repo, without the need to run a setup or to be on `gitbutler/workspace` ref.
All app operations work as normal. GitButler switches to `gitbutler/workspace` only when you apply a second parallel branch and moves back when you return to one.

## Worktree support

You can now work with linked Git worktrees directly in GitButler. Worktrees created by other apps show up in the CLI status or as lanes in the GUI and support most GitButler operations.
For example you (or your agent) can move individual changes, commits or branches to and from worktrees as needed.
Parallel branches are light & fast while worktrees offer full code isolation so each tool can be used situationally.
Worktrees that already exist when you upgrade start archived. Bring them in from the new Worktrees page in Project settings or with the `but` CLI.
Discarding changes in a worktree can’t be undone yet.


## Changes

- Projects now use a local target branch, so GitButler can be used on repos without a remote
- Faster refreshes in Git LFS repositories and after undo, plus faster workspace updates in repositories with ma

releases.name: release/0.22.3
releases.body:
## Fixes
- Fixes an incorrect GitHub or GitLab authentication error when syncing a project without a connected forge integration
- Fixes GitHub pull request publishing failures showing "422 Unprocessable Entity" instead of GitHub's explanation of what needs fixing
- Fixes a 0.22.2 regression were in some cases the app uses a fallback committer value instead of the configured Git identity

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/compare/release/0.22.2...release/0.22.3

releases.name: release/0.22.2
releases.body:
## Changes
- Updating the workspace now fast-forwards a local target branch like `main` after its remote branch advances

## Fixes
- GitHub repositories with 100 or more open pull requests now refresh correctly as pull request activity changes
- GitLab: An open merge request with no head commit no longer breaks merge request loading
- Edit mode no longer crashes on conflicts in non-UTF-8 files or treats those conflicts as resolved
- Workspace syncs no longer fail when a remote the workspace does not use cannot be fetched
- Uncommitted changes now load correctly when staged and unstaged changes overlap
- Slow fetch, push, and clone operations are no longer cancelled after two minutes
- Pull request and merge request information stays visible when GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket credentials are missing or a refresh fails due to a network error
- Onboarding no longer gets stuck when no Git identity is configured

aiSummary.oneLiner: A Git client designed for concurrent feature work using virtual branches.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: GitButler reinvents version control workflows by allowing developers to work on multiple disparate tasks simultaneously without constantly stashing or switching branches. It monitors the working directory and intelligently groups uncommitted changes into separate 'virtual branches' based on file context or manual selection. When ready, developers can push these virtual branches individually to remote servers as standard Git branches. This fundamentally eliminates the friction of managing multiple work-in-progress states. It heavily utilizes Rust for performance and integrates deeply with standard Git repositories without requiring structural changes.
keyFeatures: Virtual Branching: Groups file changes into distinct, manageable tracks without altering the underlying Git branch state.
Simultaneous Workflows: Allows seamless switching between unrelated features without the need to stash or commit half-finished work.
Intelligent Chunking: Automatically suggests grouping file modifications based on related context, paths, or semantics.
Native Integration: Pushes virtual branches directly to GitHub or GitLab, appearing as standard branches for review.
Visual Commit Management: Simplifies complex operations like squashing, splitting, and rewriting commit history visually before pushing.

useCases.title: Concurrent Feature Development
useCases.description: A developer fixing a critical bug in one file while simultaneously developing a new feature in another, without branch juggling.

useCases.title: Code Review Preparation
useCases.description: Splitting a large, sprawling set of uncommitted changes into multiple, focused pull requests for easier review.

useCases.title: Instant Context Switching
useCases.description: Immediately pausing work on a complex feature to address a colleague's question by applying a patch, then returning seamlessly.

useCases.title: History Rewriting
useCases.description: Cleaning up a messy local commit history into logical, atomic commits visually before sharing with the broader team.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: GitButler is designed for professional software engineers looking to optimize their daily Git workflows. It is especially useful for developers managing high-velocity, multi-tasking environments.
